$comment: Repository trust anchor for the eng/scripts/generate-api-baseline.ps1 NuGet downloads.
These SHA-256 hashes were established ONCE, deliberately, not on-first-download (TOFU).
Each was captured by downloading the package fresh from nuget.org, independently
verifying its NuGet author signature via eng/tools/PackageVerify (both integrity --
does the package content still match what was signed -- and certificate trust chain),
confirming isSigned=true and isValid=true for all seven, and only then recording the
resulting file hash here under review.
generate-api-baseline.ps1 treats this file as the source of truth for 'is this the
package we mean to trust': every package+version pair it downloads MUST already have
an entry here, or the script refuses to proceed. A downloaded (or cached) file whose
SHA-256 does not match its pinned entry is rejected outright, regardless of whether its
signature still verifies -- a byte-for-byte identical republish is the only thing that
should ever match. A locally cached copy is only a performance shortcut for avoiding a
redundant download; this file, not the cache, is what decides trust.
packageVersion must equal eng/baselines.json's source.behaviorBaseline.tag. If that tag
is ever bumped, this file must be regenerated (delete it, run
eng/scripts/generate-api-baseline.ps1, review the new pinned hashes in the diff, and
